column1: # aes-r2b-rlist.tsv -- AES round 2b: the window rectangle list.
# Format (seven tab separated columns):
#   opcode  n_intin  n_intout  n_addrin  n_addrout  intin values  comment
# as cases/aes-r1.tsv and cases/aes-r2-wind.tsv, and read by the same
# loader.  A '+' opcode is a PRELUDE: issued after the reset and before the
# measured call, never recorded.  A case id is the PHYSICAL LINE NUMBER and
# this file's CRC binds every dump to it, so ANY edit -- an appended case, a
# fixed typo in a comment -- invalidates every dump already taken with it.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS SEPARATELY FROM aes-r2-wind.tsv
# That table names WF_FIRSTXYWH / WF_NEXTXYWH as unmeasurable, and its
# reason is correct as far as it goes:
#   "w_owns WRITES pwin->w_rnext (gemwmlib.c:1235), so the pair is an
#    iterator: the answer depends on how many times it has been asked,
#    which a single measured call per case cannot state."
# A single *measured* call cannot -- but a case is not a single call.  The
# reset runs before every case, and the preludes then put the iterator in a
# stated position, exactly the way the wind_set cases put a slider in one.
# "How many times it has been asked" is therefore part of the case, and the
# measured call is reproducible.  What that costs is one rule, below.
# The pair is worth measuring because it is the rectangle list every GEM
# application walks to redraw itself, and because one real application
# already turns on it: QED decides between drawing directly and deferring
# by comparing WF_FIRSTXYWH against its own work rectangle
# (`free_for_draw`, sdk/apps/qed/src/window.c:267).
# THE ONE RULE: NEXT IS NEVER MEASURED WITHOUT A FIRST BEFORE IT
# w_setup (gemwmlib.c:205-228) initialises w_owner, w_flags, w_kind,
# w_pname, w_pinfo and the four slider fields.  It does NOT initialise
# w_rnext, and w_rnext is written in exactly one place in the whole AES:
# w_owns (:1235).  So on a freshly created window w_rnext still holds
# whatever the slot's previous life left there -- an ORECT pointer that
# newrect has since handed back to the free list (gemwrect.c:184,204).
# A measured WF_NEXTXYWH with no WF_FIRSTXYWH before it would therefore
# dereference a freed pointer and follow its o_link.  That is not merely
# unreproducible, it is unsafe on a machine nobody is watching.  **Every
# NEXT case in this file carries a FIRST as its prelude**, including the
# ones on handle 0: wm_new sweeps handles >= 1 only (:1886), so the
# desktop's w_rnext survives the reset and is no better defined.
# WHAT THE MEASUREMENT IS ACTUALLY FOR
# w_owns, in full (gemwmlib.c:1229-1240):
#     while (po) {
#         rc_copy(&po->o_gr, poutwds);
#         pwin->w_rnext = po = po->o_link;
#         if (rc_intersect(pt, poutwds))
#             return;
#     poutwds->g_w = poutwds->g_h = 0;
# Three things a dump can settle that reading cannot:
#   1. **The end of the list writes two words, not four.**  When the walk
#      runs out, only g_w and g_h are set to 0; g_x and g_y keep whatever
#      the last rc_copy left, and if the list was empty from the start they
#      keep whatever the caller's buffer held.  The poison is what makes
#      that visible, which is the whole reason the arrays are poisoned.
#   2. **The decomposition under an overlapping window.**  Section C opens
#      a second window across the first and walks the lower one's list.
#      How the visible remainder is cut into rectangles, and in which
#      order, is newrect/brkrct (gemwrect.c:101-205) -- the part of the
#      redraw path no source reading has ever pinned down against a real
#      machine.
#   3. **Clipping against the work area.**  w_owns intersects every
#      rectangle with w_getsize(WS_WORK), so the answers carry the border
#      arithmetic too, on a window that really exists.
# SAFETY
# Every rule enforced by core/cases.c holds here unchanged.  In addition,
# this file obeys the two limits aes-r2-wind.tsv set for itself and proved
# on both machines:
#   * only handles 1 and 2 are ever opened, and every rectangle lies
#     inside 640x400, so nothing is clipped on one machine and not the
#     other.  The two-window geometry is the one aes-r2-wind.tsv already
#   * no unpaired END_MCTRL, no wind_set on handle 0, no wind_open(0).
# Nothing here draws anything aes-r2-wind.tsv did not already draw: the
# preludes are its preludes, and wind_get itself writes no pixels.
# WHAT IS EXPECTED TO DIFFER, AND IS STILL WORTH MEASURING
#   * The work-area arithmetic inside every answer: gl_wbox / gl_hbox are
#     font metrics, the same dependency round 1 measured through
#     wind_calc.  Recorded, not compared away.
#   * WF_OWNER-style process ids do not appear here at all.
# opcode\tn_intin\tn_intout\tn_addrin\tn_addrout\tintin\tcomment
!reset
# A. One window, open and unobstructed
# The list of a window nothing overlaps is a single ORECT, so FIRST
# answers the work area and the very next NEXT is already the end.

column7: WF_FIRSTXYWH of an open, unobstructed window: its work area
walk the iterator to the single rectangle
WF_NEXTXYWH at the end: g_w/g_h are 0, g_x/g_y are NOT written
WF_NEXTXYWH past the end: po is NULL, the loop is not entered at all

column1: # B. A window that exists but was never opened
# wm_new leaves w_rlist NULL (gemwrect.c:184 gives the ORECTs back and
# newrect rebuilds only for open windows), so the walk never starts.
# Safe: po is NULL, nothing is dereferenced.

column7: WF_FIRSTXYWH of a created, unopened window: empty list

column1: # C. Two windows, the lower one partly covered
# The geometry is the one aes-r2-wind.tsv already ran on both machines:
# window 1 at 30,40,320,240 and window 2 at 60,80,200,160 on top of it.
# Window 2 covers the middle of window 1, so window 1's visible remainder
# is more than one rectangle and the iterator has something to iterate.

column7: WF_FIRSTXYWH of the covered window: the first visible piece
WF_NEXTXYWH: the second visible piece -- how brkrct cut it
the third piece, if the decomposition has one
the fourth: how many pieces there are is the measurement
WF_FIRSTXYWH of the TOP window: nothing covers it, one piece

column1: # D. The desktop's own list, handle 0
# D.w_win[0] is outside wm_new's sweep, but newrect rebuilds every
# window's list from geometry on each open and close (gemwrect.c:160-205),
# so with no window open the desktop owns one rectangle, and with one open
# it owns the remainder around it.  Its w_rnext still survives the reset,
# which is why these two cases carry a FIRST prelude like all the others.

column7: WF_FIRSTXYWH of the desktop, nothing open: the whole desktop
walk the desktop iterator to its single rectangle
WF_NEXTXYWH on the desktop at the end
WF_FIRSTXYWH of the desktop with one window open: the remainder
WF_NEXTXYWH: the next piece of the desktop remainder

column1: # E. OUT_LEN on a rectangle field
# xif copies control[OUT_LEN] words back and no more (gemsuper.c:430-432);
# the arm itself writes poutwds[0..3] through w_owns.  These two say
# whether the copy-back honours the declaration on a field whose handler
# writes four words.

column7: WF_FIRSTXYWH, OUT_LEN 1: the return code only, the rect stays poisoned
WF_FIRSTXYWH, OUT_LEN 3: x and y arrive, w and h stay poisoned
